MOHAMMAD NAWAZ, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The State has preferred this appeal against the judgment and order dated 05.02.2020 passed by the Court of the II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bagalkot, in Special Case No.453/2013,
whereby the respondent/accused has been acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 366,
376 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(xi), 3(1)(xii) and 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

sentences.text: 2. We have heard both sides and perused the evidence and material on record.

3. The brief facts of the prosecution case are that, on 15.09.2013, at about 5.00 pm, on the road near KSRTC Bus Stand, Hungund, knowing fully well that the victim girl belongs to scheduled caste, the accused kidnapped her on a Hero Honda motorcycle bearing registration No.KA29/L6774, in order that she may be forced or NC: 2024:KHC-D:8056-DB seduced to illicit intercourse and took her inside the pump-set room, situated in the land bearing R.S.No.75- A/1, beside Malaprabha river bank in Maradi Budihal village, Hungund Taluk and committed rape on her against her will and thereby committed the charged offences.
4. The complaint - Ex.P1 is lodged by the victim/PW1, wherein she has stated that she is studying in PUC-II year at Sri.V.M.S.R.V College, Hungund Town, staying in a hostel.
On 15.09.2013 at about 5.00 pm, she was proceeding to Hungund market from her hostel.

When she reached near Hungund Bus Stand circle, accused came on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 20/L-6774 and induced her saying that her mother is unwell and in the guise of taking her to the village, took her to a pump set shed situated in his land and in spite of her resistance, forcibly committed rape on her.

It is further stated that her uncles Shivalingappa Dyavappa Budihal (PW7), Gyanappa Yallappa Dodamani (PW8) and Chandrashekar Kanakappa Maganuru (PW9) came to the NC:
2024:KHC-D:8056-DB spot after coming to know about the incident and on seeing them, the accused fled away.

Thereafter, she was taken to her house and after discussing with the elders, she State Of Karnataka vs Saheblal S/O. Moulasab Chapparband on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81012701/
2 along with her uncles, went to the police station and lodged the complaint.

sentences.text: 5. The prosecution has got examined PWs. 1 to 31 and got marked Exs.P1 to P29 and M.Os.1 to 14.

The defence has got marked Exs. D1 to D3.
6.

Appreciating the oral and documentary evidence on record, the learned Sessions Judge has come to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.

7. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has mainly relied on the evidence of the victim examined as PW1, PWs.3 and 6 -parents of the victim, PWs.7 to 9 and 17 and the evidence of the doctor - PW24.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:8056-DB 8.

PW2 is the panch witness to Ex.P6 under which M.Os. 10 and 11 are seized and the photographs which are marked as Exs.P2 to P5.
9.

PWs. 4 and 5 are panch witnesses to the mahazar drawn at the spot from where accused is alleged to have abducted the victim and also for the seizure of the motorcycle, marked as Exs.P7 and P8 respectively.
PW4 has turned hostile, whereas PW7 has supported the case of prosecution.
10. PWs.10 and 11 are hearsay witnesses, who have come to know about the incident from PW7.
11. PW12 is a social worker who was informed about the incident by PW7.
He went along with the victim and others to the police station for lodging the complaint.
12. PW13 is the registered owner of the motorcycle and PW14 is the purchaser of the motorcycle.
13. PW14 has stated that he has given the land in Survey No.75-A/1 measuring 1 acre 35 guntas on lease to NC: 2024:KHC-D:8056-DB the father of the accused.
He has turned hostile insofar as the incident is concerned.
14. PW16 is the warden of the hostel where the victim was staying.
15. PWs.18 to 21, 23, 26 are the police officials who assisted the Investigation Officer in investigation.
16. PW.22 is the head master of the school who issued Ex.P13, certificate showing the date of birth and caste of the victim.
17. PW.24 is the medical officer who examined the victim and issued medical certificate as per Ex.P.15 and gave opinion on receiving the FSL report as per Ex.P.17.

PW.25 is the doctor who examined the accused and issued reports as per Exs.P18 and P19.
19.
PWs.27 and 28 are the junior engineers who prepared spot sketches, marked as Exs.P21 and P22.
PW.29 is the PSI who registered the case on receiving the complaint Ex.P1 from the victim and issued FIR-Ex.P10 to the jurisdictional court.
21. PWs.30 and 31 are the investigation officers.
22. It is well settled that victim's solitary evidence in matters related to sexual offence is generally deemed sufficient to hold an accused guilty.
However, the accused cannot be convicted if the prosecutrix testimony is found unreliable and insufficient due to identified flaws and lacunae.

To hold an accused guilty for commission of offence of rape, the solitary evidence of prosecutrix is sufficient provided the same inspires confidence and appears to be absolutely trust worthy,
unblemished and should be of sterling quality.
23. The incident is alleged to have taken place on 15.09.2013 at about 5 p.m.
It is an undisputed fact that, as on the date of incident the prosecutrix was a major.
As per the certificate issued by the school, she was aged NC: 2024:KHC-D:8056-DB about 18 years 5 months.
In her cross examination PW.1- victim has admitted that she was aged 18 years 5 months as on the date of incident.
24. As per prosecution, the victim was studying in II PUC at one Sri.VMSRV college, Hungund town and she was staying in a hostel.

In Ex.P1, she has stated that while she was proceeding to Hungund market and when she was near Hungund bus stand circle, the accused came on a motorcycle and telling her that her mother is unwell and in the guise of taking her to the village, took her on his motorcycle to the pump set shed situated in his rented land and committed forcible sexual intercourse on her.
25. In her deposition, PW.1 has stated that after taking her to the pump set shed, accused dragged her by hand, pulled her and she screamed.
He tied her hands and legs and gagged her mouth with the help of her vale, lit a lamp and committed rape on her.

It is relevant to see that the complaint was lodged on the next date i.e. on NC: 2024:KHC-D:8056-DB 16.09.2013 at about 1 p.m., however,
in Ex.P1 there is no whisper about the accused tying her hands and legs with a vale and gagging her mouth.
In her cross examination, she has stated that both the families were known to each other.
She has admitted that neither in Ex.P1 or in her further statement she has stated that accused tied her hands and legs and gagged her mouth.
It is also relevant to see that at the time of conducting the spot mahazar, M.Os. 10 and 11 were seized.
M.O.10 is the mud lamp and M.O.11 is the rold-gold small chain belonging to the victim.
There is no mention about the same in Ex.P1.
PW.1 has admitted in her cross examination that she has not mentioned the same in Ex.P1 or in her further statement.

sentences.text: It is the case of prosecution that PWs.7, 8, 9 and 17 came in search of the victim and they saw both the victim and accused together inside the pump set shed and while they tried to nab the accused, he escaped from the spot.

Thereafter, victim was brought to her house and on the next day complaint was lodged.
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:8056-DB 27.
We have carefully examined the evidence of PWs.7, 8, 9 and 17.
The said witnesses are the uncles of the victim.

According to the PW.7, on the date of incident at about 5.40 p.m., he along with PWs.8 and 9 was standing at Kudalasangam cross and at that time they saw the accused taking the victim on his motorcycle towards their village.
Therefore, they followed them on two motorcycles.
They noticed the motorcycle of the accused parked near the water tank.

When they searched for them,
they noticed accused and the victim inside the shed.
On seeing them accused came out of the shed and ran away.
Similar is the evidence of PWs.8, and 9.

However, it is pertinent to see that the said witnesses have not spoken about the presence of PW.17, wherein PW.17 has deposed that on 15.09.2013 at about 5.30 pm he was informed by PW.7 over the phone that accused has kidnapped the victim telling her that her mother is unwell and called him.
Accordingly, he went to Sangam cross, wherein PW.7 was present.
Thereafter, they saw accused taking the victim on his motorcycle and therefore, he along with PW.7 followed - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:8056-DB them and then found both of them inside the shed.
On seeing them, the accused ran away.
He has stated that half an hour after reaching the spot, PWs.8 and 9 came to the spot.
28. If the evidence of PW.17 is appreciated, it is clear that PWs.8 and 9 came to the spot half an hour after the accused ran away from the spot.

29. It is the specific case of the prosecution that the accused told the victim that her mother is unwell and in the guise of taking her to her village took her on his motorcycle to the shed situated in his rented land and committed forcible sexual intercourse on her.
In Ex.P1, PW.1 has stated that while she was proceeding to Hungund market from her hostel, accused came in the motorcycle and in the guise of taking her to the village took her on his motorcycle.
She has nowhere stated that she obtained permission from the warden to leave the hostel.
The prosecution has examined PW.16-Hostel warden, according to whom the victim had given leave note stating - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:8056-DB that she is going to her village on 18.09.2013.
PW.16 has stated that she has seen the accused earlier when he had come to the hostel to visit the victim.
She has further admitted that earlier victim had taken her permission to meet the accused and she has seen the State Of Karnataka vs Saheblal S/O. Moulasab Chapparband

30. PWs.7, 8 and 9 have deposed in their evidence that when they went to the shed, the accused and the victim were sitting together.
PW.9 has admitted that both of them were sitting close to each other by lighting a lamp and seeing them both of them got panic.
PW.1 got scared and came out of the shed.
He has admitted that PWs.7 and 8 assaulted the victim asking her why she has came to the shed along with the accused.
31. PWs.3 and 6 are the parents of the victim.
They were informed about the incident by PWs.7 to 9.

PW.3 in his cross examination has admitted that, he along with the father of the accused have taken the land on lease from its owner for a sum of Rs.36,000/- and they were cultivating - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:8056-DB the land and equally sharing the usufructs.
He admitted that in this connection they were not in talking terms.

He has further admitted that they discussed about the matter and none from the side of the accused came for a discussion and in case they had come for the discussion, they were ready to settle the matter.

The suggestion put to him that they demanded Rs.2,00,000/- from the accused for settling the matter and since they refused to pay the said amount a false complaint was filed, has been denied.
32.
PW.6-mother of the victim has stated that she has not given any statement to the Police pertaining to the case.

In her statement, she has stated that they were informed about the incident by PWs.7 to 9.
33.

A careful perusal of the evidence of PWs.7 to 9 and 17 who have gone to the spot and noticed both the accused and victim together inside the shed does not indicate that any such incident as alleged by the prosecution has taken place.
Whereas their evidence - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:8056-DB clearly disclose that, the accused and victim were sitting close to each other inside the shed.

34. It is contended by the learned counsel for the respondent that even accepting the evidence of PW.1, it cannot be said that the accused has kidnapped the victim and then committed forcible sexual intercourse on her.

He contended that from the evidence of PWs.7 to 9, it is clear that victim herself accompanied the accused on his motorcycle and went to the shed on her own and when PWs.7 to 9 followed them and came near the shed and saw them sitting together and chatting, she became panic.
He further contended that, at the instance of PWs.7 to 9 and PW.12, a social worker, a false complaint was lodged on the next day.
35. Learned counsel for the respondent has also contended that, PW9 has admitted they went to the police station on the very same night and met the PSI, but no complaint was lodged.

We have State Of Karnataka vs Saheblal S/O. Moulasab Chapparband on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81012701/
6 perused the said cross- examination of PW-9 wherein, he has admitted that at 11 - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:8056-DB p.m., on the very same night, they went the police station and met the PSI.

sentences.text: He has further admitted that even a complaint was lodged.
However, it is pertinent to see that as per Ex.P-1, complaint was lodged at 1.00 p.m. on 16.09.2013.
It is not forthcoming as to what was the complaint lodged on the same night.
36. Learned counsel for the respondent has also drawn the attention of the Court to the evidence of PW-12, a Social Worker.
A perusal of his evidence shows that on 16.09.2013 when he was in his house, PW-7 came along with PW-1-victim, who informed him about the incident.
He has stated that all of them went to the police station and PW-1 lodged the complaint.

It is contended by the learned counsel that as per the cross-examination conducted by the defence, PW12 has admitted that he is an office bearer of 'Madigara Horata Samiti' of their area who is having close association with the police officers.
Hence, it is contended that at his instance, a false complaint was lodged.

The learned Addl. SPP has contended that the evidence of PW-1 is corroborated by medical evidence, wherein PW-24 who examined PW-1 has noticed certain injuries and he has also noticed that hymen was not intact.
Hence, he contended that the evidence of PW1 is trustworthy and believable.

38. As per Ex.P-15, medical report of PW1, issued by PW24, hymen is absent, at the vaginal introitus to the posterior aspect there was a small abrasion of about 1 x 0.5 cm of more than 12 hours duration, but does not prove whether forcefully or with willing.

On face, right side of the mouth 2 linear scratch marks seen parallel to each other, below the neck towards left side of the above left breast small scratch mark seen and redness was present along lateral wall of the vaginal introitus which indicates
that intercourse has occurred.
39. PW-24 has deposed in her evidence that she cannot say whether the intercourse was willful or forceful and as per Ex.P-17, no seminal stains were found.

She - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:8056-DB has admitted that the victim girl has not stated that she had undergone forceful sexual intercourse and therefore, history of examination was not recorded in Ex.P-15.
She has admitted that sexual intercourse might have taken place with the consent of victim girl.
As per FSL reports- Exs.P-28 and P-29, presence of seminal stains were not detected in the samplings collected from the victim and her clothes.

sentences.text: The trial Court having examined the evidence of material witnesses namely PW-1, PW-3, PW-5 to PW-9, PW-13, PW-14, PW-16, PW-17, PW-24 and PW-25 and after giving reasons has come to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to substantiate its version and the evidence of PW-1 does not inspire the confidence of the Court to base conviction against the accused.
41. Having re-appreciated the entire evidence and material on record, we find that the findings recorded by the trial Court are in accordance with law.

It is well settled that in an appeal preferred against a judgment of - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:8056-DB acquittal, the appellate Court shall be slow in reversing the said findings, unless the material evidence has been ignored by the trial Court.

By an order of acquittal,
innocence of the accused is re-
inforced.
Further, if two views are possible from the evidence on record, the view favorable to the accused should be taken.
Considering the reasons assigned by the trial Court and on re-appraisal of the evidence, we are of the considered view that, the view taken by the trial Court is a plausible view.
Hence, appeal fails and accordingly, dismissed.
